post.caption:
Light entering glass at a shallow enough angle undergoes total internal reflection: it hits the boundary and bounces straight back in, over and over, all the way down the fibre. The glass is pure enough that a signal survives around a hundred kilometres before needing a repeater, and each strand carries terabits per second. Hundreds of those cables lie on the seafloor right now. The cloud is a rope of glass in the dark.
